newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police question MP on Brotherhood suspicion.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police question MP on Brotherhood suspicion.

text.p: Egyptian state security investigators on Sunday began questioning an Islamist MP they suspect is a member of the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood, security sources said.
They said Labour Party member Ali Sayyed Fath al-Bab could face charges of setting up a secret organisation and taking part in criminal activity aimed at creating instability in Egypt.
If proven guilty the maximum penalty for al-Bab would be life imprisonment with hard labour, the security sources said.
Egypt's parliament lifted Fath al-Bab's immunity last month so that investigators could query him. Police suspect he was involved with a group of 53 alleged Brotherhood members.

The Brotherhood has denounced Fath al-Bab's arrest and said it was aimed at barring Islamists from parliament. Fath al-Bab is the only parliamentarian who belongs to the opposition Labour party, which has Islamist tendencies.
The Labour Party contains many members of the Brotherhood, which repeatedly has been denied legal recognition as a political party.

For many years the state tolerated the Brotherhood, Egypt's largest and most influential Moslem organisation, but for the past two years it has tried to equate it with the violent groups trying to overthrow the government by force.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since 1992 when Moslem militant groups began their armed struggle for power but Brotherhood leaders say they oppose the use of violence for political ends.
